<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dmpt-2016-0029_s_999_w2aab2b8c23b1b7b1aab1c14b1Aa">
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Cytochrome P450-2D6 (CYP2D6), a member of the CYP450 mixed function oxidase system, is an important CYP isoform with regard to herbal-drug interactions and is responsible for the metabolism of nearly 25% of drugs. Until now, studies on the effects of various phytochemicals on CYP2D6 activity
                      <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                      have been very rare. Gallic acid and ellagic acid are natural polyphenols which are widely distributed in fruits and medicinal plants. In the present study, the effects of gallic acid and ellagic acid pretreatment on intestinal transport and oral bioavailability of metoprolol were investigated.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dmpt-2016-0029_s_998_w2aab2b8c23b1b7b1aab1c14b2Aa">
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The intestinal transport of metoprolol was assessed by conducting an
                      <jats:italic>in situ</jats:italic>
                      single pass intestinal perfusion (SPIP) study. The bioavailability study was conducted to evaluate the pharmacokinetic parameters of orally administered metoprolol in rats.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dmpt-2016-0029_s_997_w2aab2b8c23b1b7b1aab1c14b3Aa">
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      After pretreatment with gallic acid and ellagic acid, no significant change in effective permeability of metoprolol was observed at the ileum part of rat intestine. A significant improvement in the peak plasma concentration (C
                      <jats:sub>max</jats:sub>
                      ) and area under the serum concentration–time profile (AUC) and decrease in clearance were observed in rats pretreated with gallic acid and ellagic acid.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="j_dmpt-2016-0029_s_996_w2aab2b8c23b1b7b1aab1c14b4Aa">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Gallic acid and ellagic acid significantly enhanced the oral bioavailability of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6-mediated metabolism in the rat liver. Hence, adverse herbal-drug interactions may result with concomitant ingestion of gallic acid and ellagic acid supplements and drugs that are CYP2D6 substrates. The clinical assessment of these interactions should be further investigated in human volunteers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Enhanced oral bioavailability of metoprolol with gallic acid and ellagic acid in male Wistar rats: involvement of CYP2D6 inhibition
